mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% in a month signals tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% in three months indicates a tightening labor market, which increases wage costs and reduces corporate profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in real GDP by more than 2% in a quarter signals strong economic growth, which boosts corporate earnings and consumer spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production by more than 1% in a month signals a contraction in supply, which can lead to increased prices and reduced corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts by more than 5% over three months signals increased demand for housing, which boosts related industries and consumer spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is above 2% and the CPI is increasing by more than 0.5% per month, the combined effect of high interest rates and inflationary pressure reduces corporate earnings and consumer purchasing power, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 2% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls increase by more than 200,000 in a month and the unemployment rate decreases by more than 0.3%, it signals a strong labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases > 200,000 and UNRATE decreases > 0.3% in 1 month
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real retail and food services sales by more than 1% per month for three consecutive months signals strong consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of instances despite the positive signal.
